text: Bujar Faik Nishani (Albanian pronunciation: [bujaɾ ni'ʃani]; 29 September 1966 – 28 May 2022) was an Albanian politician who served as the president of Albania from 24 July 2012 to 24 July 2017. He was the youngest person ever elected to the presidency, taking office at the age of 47. Before becoming president, Nishani held several governmental and diplomatic roles, including Minister of Internal Affairs from 2007 to 2009 and again between 2011 and 2012, and Minister of Justice from 2009 to 2011. Born in Durrës, Albania, on 29 September 1966, to teachers with roots from Gjirokastër, he was a distant relative of Omer Nishani, Chairman of the Presidium of the People's Socialist Republic of Albania, but changed his surname to Mehmeti during the communist era. He graduated from the Skanderbeg Military University in 1988 and earned a master's degree in "defense resources management" from the Naval Postgraduate School in the United States in 1996. In 2004, he graduated from the Law Faculty of the University of Tirana, where he studied jurisprudence, and completed a master's degree in European studies in 2005. After the fall of communism in 1991, he joined the Democratic Party of Albania (DP). In 1992, he became an expert and Director of Foreign Relations at the Ministry of Defense, later moving to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in 1994 to coordinate the NATO Relations Office. In 1996, he served as Chief of Staff to Safet Zhulali, Minister of Defense, until the DP lost the 1997 parliamentary election. In 2001, he was elected general secretary of the DP's branch in Tirana and won a seat in the Tirana Municipal Council in the 2003 local election. He became a member of the DP's National Council in 2005 and later joined the party's central presidency. He won a seat for Tirana's 34th constituency in the 2005 parliamentary election, defeating then Minister of Interior Igli Toska, and was re-elected in 2009. He became Minister of Interior on 20 March 2007, holding the position until 17 September 2009, and was then appointed Minister of Justice from 17 September 2009 to 25 April 2011. Following the resignation of Lulzim Basha as Minister of Interior to run for Mayor of Tirana, Nishani was appointed again as Minister of Interior until June 2012. On 10 June 2012, the day before the fourth round of presidential voting in Parliament, the governing coalition discussed new candidates; although initially proposing Artan Hoxha as the ruling party's candidate, Hoxha withdrew due to opposition, and the coalition then proposed Nishani. In the parliamentary session, Nishani won the vote with 73 votes, all from the governing coalition, while opposition deputies, including those from the Socialist Party, did not participate. He was sworn in on 24 July 2012, becoming the youngest president in Albania's history, and in his inaugural speech announced that his priority was judicial reform and Albania's integration into the European Union. His first state visit abroad was to Kosovo in August 2012, where he expressed support for Kosovo's independence as irreversible and emphasized the need for dialogue with Serbia. In 2013, he did not attend the South-East European Cooperation Process summit in Macedonia due to Serbia's objection to the absence of the Kosovo president. In 2016, he called on the United Nations to recognize Kosovo's independence. On 16 November 2012, he received the body of King Zog I, who had died in exile over 50 years earlier. In July 2013, he called for a referendum on trash imports, held on 22 December. In August 2013, he transferred ownership of a large building in Tirana from the Albanian Armed Forces to the Democratic Party of Albania for its new headquarters, despite opposition from Xhemal Gjunkshi. After the September 2013 parliamentary election, he appointed Edi Rama as Prime Minister. In November 2013, he urged the President of Greece, Karolos Papoulias, to abolish the 1940 declaration of war against Albania, seeking to resolve the Cham issue, and stated Albania was ready to resolve maritime border disputes with Greece according to international law. In 2014, he criticized the lack of transparency in the approval of laws on the armed forces and the Defense Intelligence and Security Agency and rejected judicial reform, arguing it should be led by judges, not politicians. In May 2015, following protests in Macedonia that resulted in deaths, he called for a swift and complete investigation into the incident. On 17 December 2015, the parliament passed a law barring individuals with criminal records for serious offenses from holding public office, and Nishani issued a decree to take effect immediately upon parliamentary approval. In April 2016, he opposed a government law equating citizenship with arms, calling it "inadequate" and "not positive." The election of nine new Supreme Court judges on 26 June 2016 sparked controversy, as five judges accused Nishani and the president of the Supreme Court of violating legal procedures. At the 71st UN General Assembly in September 2016, during his final address, he stated Albania would address global challenges through cooperation, including increasing humanitarian aid, ratifying the Paris Agreement on climate change, and fulfilling commitments in the security sector. His foreign policy emphasized strengthening good-neighborly relations and supporting Kosovo's participation in multilateral activities. His term ended on 24 July 2017, succeeded by Ilir Meta, who won the 2017 Albanian presidential election. Nishani was married to Odeta Nishani, with whom he had two children, a son Ersi and a daughter Fiona. He was fluent in English, a Muslim, and on 21 April 2017 became the first Albanian president to make a pilgrimage to Mecca. In 2008, he underwent surgery for a cerebral cavernoma and resumed duties as Minister of Interior just two weeks later. In 2022, he was admitted to hospital for pneumonia complications from post-COVID-19 fibrosis, transferred to Germany on 23 April for specialized treatment, and died in Berlin, Germany at 7 a.m. (06 UTC) on 28 May 2022, at the age of 55. On 31 May, his body arrived in Albania via a hearse crossing the Kosovo-Albania border at Morina, was laid in state at the Presidential Palace, and the government declared 2 June a day of national mourning. His state funeral took place on that day from 10:00 to 12:00, and he was buried in the Sharra public cemetery in Tirana.
